note: Hand-written and human-reviewed. One central experiment per investigation: the object a reader acts on, the control they move, the quantity that comes back, where the evidence lands, the steps of the loop, and the browser test that drives it end to end. `npm run audit:scene:check` refuses to pass if any of those six names something the lesson no longer has. It cannot judge whether the experiment is a good one, and does not claim to. Nothing here is a claim about learning gains: no study has been run.
objectForms: A role the lesson binds or stages, the literal "the selected body", or "panel:<widget-id>" for a lesson whose central experiment is a panel model with nothing on the canvas. It can also be "compute:<notebook id>" for a lesson whose experiment is run on the compute page; some step must then declare the same notebook with `compute: "<notebook id>"` (Roadmap II Prompt 102).
controlForms: "<widget-id>/<control-id>" is checked against the registry. Anything else is prose, for an affordance that lives in the application's own panels rather than in a lesson widget.

keplers-laws.control: the canvas: click a body, then Run and the event watch
keplers-laws.quantity: semi-major axis a and period P for four planets

retrograde-motion.control: the inspector: select Earth and switch on Reference frame

transit-photometry.quantity: transit depth, and the planet radius it implies

orbital-energy.quantity: the dividing speed, as the last speed on each side of it

weighing-stars.quantity: two arm lengths and one period, giving both masses

black-holes.quantity: Schwarzschild radius against mass, captured at three masses

radial-velocity.quantity: the semi-amplitude K, and the minimum mass it gives

missing-mass.quantity: orbital speed against radius, measured and then fitted

tides.quantity: tidal acceleration at four distances and three masses

butterfly-effect.control: the experiment bench: Set up and run both
butterfly-effect.quantity: separation between two runs, and its e-folding time

when-orbits-lock.control: the sandbox: run, and the resonance panels read the scene
when-orbits-lock.quantity: the Laplace argument, and the amplitude it librates through

detect-this-planet.quantity: detection significance for two observing schedules

design-the-schedule.control: the schedule workspace: set the cadence and run both
design-the-schedule.quantity: the period recovered from each schedule, and its alias

binary-star-planets.control: the experiment bench: run the separation sweep
binary-star-planets.quantity: whether the planet survives twenty binary periods, against separation

gravity-assist.control: the inspector: read speed in two frames, before and after

hohmann-transfer.control: the maneuver planner: transverse burn, then Apply
hohmann-transfer.quantity: the top and bottom of the arc after the first burn

lagrange-points.control: the sandbox: place a tracer and run it in the rotating frame
lagrange-points.quantity: the Jacobi constant, and whether the neck is open

what-is-a-gravitational-wave.quantity: whether each of three sources emits, and the ring's change in length

listening-to-spacetime.quantity: time in band, and peak strain, against mass and distance

a-universe-of-stars.quantity: temperature, luminosity and the radius ratio they imply

lives-of-stars.quantity: radius and luminosity at a stated model age

twelve-nights.quantity: the spectral window power at the sidereal day, for two placements of the same twelve nights

power-law-gravity.quantity: apsidal precession in degrees per radial period, at four exponents

color-and-temperature.quantity: the peak wavelength at three temperatures, and its product with the temperature

the-turning-sky.quantity: the time a star rises on night 0 and night 30, and the sidereal time at midnight

the-sun-through-the-year.quantity: the Sun’s altitude at noon at the equinox and the two solstices

phases-and-eclipses.quantity: the lit fraction of the Moon at four ages

wanderers-on-the-sky.quantity: the first days of retrograde and of direct motion for Mars

plan-a-night.quantity: the hours of astronomical dark on two nights

lines-and-motion.quantity: the Doppler velocity of two synthetic stars from their H-alpha lines, one receding and one approaching

what-a-spectrum-is-made-of.quantity: the brightness at the H-alpha center against the source's, with the same cloud cooler than the source (a dark line) and hotter (a bright line)

the-suns-motion.quantity: the Sun's U, V and W against the mean of the stars within the distance limit, with their uncertainties

the-rotating-disk.quantity: the Oort constants A and B from Gaia proper motions, with the stars weighted by distance and all alike

cluster-membership.quantity: the number of stars above a membership-probability threshold, and the cluster's proper motion

who-gets-counted.quantity: the number of stars a survey counts, and the share of the population, at a magnitude limit

why-the-bright-ones-win.quantity: the Malmquist bias: how much brighter the counted stars are than the stars there are, in shells of distance

the-completeness-curve.quantity: the share of the true luminosity function a raw count recovers, and the corrected value

bending-light.quantity: the bending of a ray of light, in arcseconds, as the closest approach changes

einstein-rings-and-arcs.quantity: the Einstein radius of a lens, in milliarcseconds, as the mass inside it changes

a-lens-passing-by.quantity: the peak brightening of a star as a lens passes, as the closest approach changes

inside-a-star.quantity: the mean density of a star, as its mass changes at a fixed radius

scaling-the-main-sequence.quantity: the luminosity exponent a scaling argument predicts, as the opacity law changes

the-limit.quantity: the radius of a white dwarf in kilometers, as its central density changes

the-beat-of-a-star.quantity: the highest period-search peak of a variable star, whole run against seen once a night

leavitts-law.control: the Galaxy selector, which slides the fitted line onto another galaxy’s Cepheids; the calibration itself has no control
leavitts-law.quantity: the slope and zero point of the Cepheid relation, and the distance a galaxy’s Cepheids give

the-first-rung.quantity: the distance modulus of a galaxy from sliding the Cepheid relation onto its Cepheids

which-kind-of-variable.quantity: the share of variable stars classified correctly as the classifier is given more measurements

the-expanding-universe.quantity: the slope through the origin of velocity against distance for the supernovae, out to z = 0.1 against out to z = 0.5

standard-candles.quantity: the Hubble constant implied by an error in the supernovae’s absolute magnitude

the-shape-of-expansion.quantity: the chi-square of the flat Lambda-CDM curve above the best fit, for a matter density you set

where-galaxies-live.quantity: the variance over mean of the galaxy counts in cells, and the galaxies shown, for the range you set

what-a-ccd-records.quantity: the net light of star B in electrons, raw and after dividing by the flat, for the frame shown

signal-noise-and-exposure.quantity: the signal-to-noise of a V = 15 star for the exposure you set

a-variable-star-from-frames.quantity: the scatter of the check star and the mean of the variable against the comparison, for the calibration applied

integrators-in-practice.control: the compute page's steps-per-period setting (not a lesson widget)
integrators-in-practice.quantity: the energy drift of explicit Euler, symplectic Euler, velocity Verlet and Runge-Kutta 4 over three periods of the widest orbit, and how each changes when the step is halved

extending-an-experiment.control: the compute page's cutoff and slope settings (not a lesson widget)
extending-an-experiment.quantity: the half-way starting distance and the bound fraction of the twenty trials and of the synthetic population, for the settings run

refitting-a-transit.control: the compute page's limb-darkening setting (not a lesson widget)
refitting-a-transit.quantity: the fitted period, planet-to-star radius ratio, orbit size, impact parameter and reduced chi-square, the covariance sigma and profile intervals, and how the radius ratio and its sigma change when the limb darkening is held fixed

two-periodograms.control: the compute page's maximum period and maximum duration settings (not a lesson widget)
two-periodograms.quantity: the best period of a Lomb-Scargle and of a box least squares periodogram of one light curve, their ratio, and the box period against the fitted period in the fit's uncertainties

sampling-a-posterior.control: the compute page's steps setting (not a lesson widget)
sampling-a-posterior.quantity: the median and 68 percent interval width of the planet-to-star radius ratio and the impact parameter from an ensemble sampler, and the convergence diagnostics that let the interval be quoted

what-is-a-measurement.quantity: the standard error of the mean of the marks of one star, which falls as the number of marks grows

what-does-plus-minus-claim.quantity: the share of seeded repeats whose stated interval holds the true value, at one and at two sigma

when-the-method-must-refuse.quantity: the chi-square of the best fit at a trial mass, which is zero above the product and rises below it

measuring-the-moon.quantity: the diameter in kilometers of a circle drawn on the Galileo picture of the Moon, from the scale a reference pair of known length sets

how-far-is-that-star.quantity: the chi-square of a fit to fourteen positions of one star: enormous for a straight line that leaves the parallax out, near its degrees of freedom once the parallax is in

a-binary-stars-orbit.quantity: the mass sum of a visual binary from its fitted orbit, which goes as the cube of the distance and so as the inverse cube of the parallax

weighing-jupiter.quantity: the period a sinusoid fitted to one moon's measured distances from Jupiter gives when the frames are taken once a night, which for Io is the alias near 2.30 days and not its own 1.77

why-venus-is-hot.quantity: the equilibrium temperature a planet's distance and Bond albedo give, beside the temperature measured at its surface: Venus 229 K against 737 K, cooler than Earth's 254 K

two-greenhouse-models.quantity: the ground temperature a single absorbing layer gives Venus as its emissivity rises, which tops out at 2^(1/4) times its equilibrium temperature, 272 K, against a measured 737 K

how-hot-is-the-day-side.quantity: the brightness temperature one band of a synthetic hot Jupiter gives, 2094 K for a planet with no absorbing band and 1780 K where one band absorbs, from an eclipse depth with the reflected light assumed none

phases-and-albedo.quantity: how well a Lambert sphere describes a synthetic phase curve: a chi-square near 31 for 23 degrees of freedom for a Lambert planet and near 82 for a Lommel-Seeliger planet, for which no albedo is returned

which-surface-is-older.quantity: the craters at least a chosen diameter across in a lunar highland and a lunar mare, per area, and the density ratio with its interval: 40 and 7 above 30 km, a ratio of 6.4 from 2.8 to 16.9

craters-by-size.quantity: the number of craters in a power-law fit of the cumulative size-frequency plot, and its index with an interval, as the smallest diameter fitted rises: the Martian highland has 91 craters above 20 km and 31 above 40 km

what-a-crater-diameter-is-worth.quantity: the uncertainty of a crater diameter from where its rim is, a fraction of the diameter that the reader sets, which dominates the quadrature sum with the scale, the circle's placement and the view: 5.0 percent of 5.3

the-turning-sun.quantity: the sidereal rotation rate of the spot group G1 from the marks of the first day chosen to the ninth, with its uncertainty: 14.13 from six days (the first day 1) and 14.04 from five (the first day 2), degrees a day

the-suns-power.quantity: the Sun's luminosity from the first days of the TSIS-1 TIM series corrected to one astronomical unit, in units of 1e26 W: 3.829 from two days and 3.828 from six

the-gaps-in-the-belt.quantity: the depletion of a Jupiter resonance window of the numbered-asteroid catalog (H below 13) against a smooth baseline fitted outside the windows, in percent: 88.0 at the 3:1 window and 63.3 at the 5:2

how-fast-does-it-spin.quantity: the rotation period of a synthetic light curve by the two-maxima rule, in hours: 6.199 for target A and 8.002 for target C over five dense nights

moons-of-the-giants.quantity: the period a sinusoid fitted to one moon's measured distances from Jupiter gives, from which the Laplace combination of three motions follows: Io 1.7682, Europa 3.5480 and Ganymede 7.1413 days, a combination of 0.015 against an uncertainty of 0.025 degrees a day

the-scale-of-the-solar-system.control: the canvas: scroll to zoom out to Neptune, and read the distances in the readout
the-scale-of-the-solar-system.quantity: the distance of Neptune from the Sun in astronomical units, 30.07, and the light time it gives, 4.17 hours

comets-and-the-sun.control: the canvas: watch the model comets, and read the first one's closest and furthest distance in the readout
comets-and-the-sun.quantity: the closest and furthest distance of the first model comet from the Sun, 5.79 and 17.84 astronomical units, and its bare-body temperature at each end

what-is-in-this-field.quantity: the sources a detector lists in one synthetic frame of forty stars as its threshold falls: 30 at 4 sigma, none of them noise, and 44 at 2.5 sigma, seven of them only noise

why-rings.quantity: the rigid Roche limit of a pair from its two densities: Phobos about Mars 5,466 km, Shoemaker-Levy 9 about Jupiter 117,327 km, and Phobos's orbit at 9,376 km lying between the rigid and the fluid limit

tides-that-move-the-moon.quantity: the Moon's distance in a constant-Q model a given time on: 62.9 Earth radii in half a billion years and 65.1 in one billion, against the 60.3 of today

ios-fire.quantity: the tidal heating of Io at k2 = 1.5 and Q = 100, 9.33 x 10^13 W at its eccentricity of 0.0041 and four times that when the eccentricity is doubled

what-a-telescope-resolves.quantity: the dip between two stars 1 arcsecond apart, in percent of the light at a star, with 0.6 arcseconds of seeing: 0 at 10 cm and 50.3 at 40 cm
